Compared with expected paleomagnetic directions from the stable India and Eurasia blocks, significant
crustal shortening of 1400±600km and 2000±550km respectively may have occurred between the
southernmarginofEurasiaandthestableIndia,andwithinEurasiasincethecollisionofIndiaandEurasia.

TheLhasablockisthesouthernmostEurasiablock,betweenthe
Yarlung–ZangbosuturetothesouthandtheBangongsuturetothe
north. The Lizizong volcanic rocks (∼65–45Ma) are widely distrib-
utedintheLhasablockalongYarlung–Zangbosuture.Onthebasisof
thedetailedmappinganderuptionhiatuses,thesevolcanicsequences
can be subdivided into lower Dianzhong (64.4–60.6Ma), middle
Nianbo (∼54Ma) and upper Pana Formations (Mo et al., 2007).
40Ar/39Ar dating on andesite and plagioclase from the Dianzhong
Fmvolcanicrocksgivesaplateauagerangingfrom64.5to60.6Ma
(Maluski et al., 1982). Zhou et al. (2004) reported a 40Ar/39Ar
plateauageof56.5MafortheNianboolivinetrachyandesiteinthe
mid-partsoftheFormation.40Ar/39Ardatinggivesanagerangeof50
to40.8MaforthePanaFmrhyoliticrocks(Moetal.,2003;Zhouetal.,
2004).TheseFormationshaveamaximumthicknessof∼5kmand
overlyunconformablytheUpperCretaceousandoldermarineand
continental sedimentary strata, and are overlain with angular un-
conformity by the Oligocene Rigongla Formation (K–Ar: 31.4Ma)
(BGMRX,1993;Mo,etal.,2007),indicatingtheageoffoldingofthe
LizizongvolcanicsispriortotheOligocene.
TheNianboFormationhasathicknessofapproximately∼1400m
in the sampled section. Fifteen sites from the Nianbo Formation,
which mainly consists of layered rhyolitic tuffs intercalated with
tuffaceous sandstone and mudstone, were sampled at Mendui area
(30°5.054′N/90°55.97′E)locatedto∼60kmtothenorthwestofLhasa
City(Figs.1Band2A,B).Orientedhandsamplesweretakenbecauseit
islogisticallydifficulttocollectpaleomagneticcoresamplesfromthe
rhyolitictuffsusingaportablegasolinedrillingmachinesatheightof
5000m. Specimens were cored from the sample block in the
laboratory. Hand samples were oriented with a magnetic compass.
Sun compass orientations were not measured because of cloudy
weather. We used the International Geomagnetic Reference Field
IGRF (2007) declination of 0.1° in the Mendui region to correct for
magnetic deviation. Each site comprised five to eleven blocks
distributedoverstratigraphic distances rangingup to 5–10m. Each
samplewithinthesiteswascollectedfromdifferentlayeredrhyolitic
tuff(Fig.2A,B)andthestudiedsectionsdisplayvolcanicrocks,which
show significantly different color and structures. The outcrop of
Nianbo Formation has homoclinal dips. The bedding in the studied
sectiondipsatsome15–35°towardstheN.Wetherefore,assumethat
each sample within one site may represent one cooling units. In
addition,onefreshrhyolitictuffsamplewascollectedatthemiddle
of the studied section for dating the Nianbo Formation volcanic
sequencesbyaconventionalAr–Armethod.

The various rhyolitic tuff layers are arranged in a simple
homoclinalsequenceandeachsamplewithinonesitewascollected
fromdifferentlayeredrhyolitictuff.Somesites(sites6,11,12,and13)
exhibitdualpolaritymagnetizationwithinthesite(Table3).Thus,we
assume that each sample is a separate cooling unit and each site
comprisesatleastseveralcoolingunits.Consequentlythemeanofthe
14sitesfromthestudiedsectionalmostcertainlyprovidesadequate
averaging of the geomagnetic field. The virtual geomagnetic
pole(VGP)scatterof18.3°forthesamplingareafallsnearthelimit
(17.6–24.9°) of predicted VGP (McFadden et al. 1991) for 30–40°
latitude and the 45–80Ma interval. This suggests that the overall
meandirectionoftheHTChasadequatelyaveragedanygeomagnetic
secularvariation.

a =9.3°; Watson and Enkin, 1993), which is statistically indistin-
